inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average implied by H1 FY2026 diluted EPS (GBP119.8m / 36.9p = 324.7m); issued share capital 321.24m at 30 June 2026. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks are de minimis (GBP0.7m H1 FY2026, GBP2.3m FY2025) so the flat count is a modelling convention the company funds only partly in cash.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash flow statement share-based payment add-back per Metrics.csv (GBP16.1m); equity-award taxes nil since FY2021. SBC is ~0.4% of revenue -- immaterial, so house and street bases nearly coincide.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts GBP/share to pence/share. No dual listing to parity-check; identity conversion, no market rate involved. Check: FY2025 diluted EPS GBP0.882 = 88.2p as printed in the filing.
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP-denominated flows discounted at a GBP-built rate: 10-year gilt ~4.5% + 5.5% UK ERP x beta 1.0 = ~10% cost of equity; debt is ~3% of capital (GBP275m facility drawdown at H1 FY2026 against a ~GBP3.9bn market cap) at ~6% pre-tax, so WACC rounds to 10.0%. The same 10% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality is priced in the bear/base/bull flows and their weights, not stacked on the discount rate (adaptations rule f). No small-cap or illiquidity premium -- FTSE 100 constituent.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. IFRS 16 lease liability of GBP14.5m at 30 June 2026 is included in total_debt (275.0 bank loans + 14.5 leases = 289.5); lease principal (GBP5.1m FY2025) is NOT deducted from the flows and lease_cost_pct_path is omitted. Immaterial either way (~1.5p/share).
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- no non-controlling interests; all profit attributable to Persimmon shareholders.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build (Drivers route), with the cyclical adaptations from owner-fcf-adaptations.md. Routed via SKILL.md row 'Operating company, cyclical: industrials/consumer' -- Persimmon is a UK volume housebuilder whose value is the stream of cash from completions, not a land-bank NAV play (the 'land subdivider' row was considered and rejected: Persimmon turns its land into completed homes at a ~1.2x inventory/revenue ratio and reports ROCE as its primary metric). First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry. CYCLICALITY HANDLING: (1) margins are ramped from the FY2026 consensus-implied ~12.6% EBITDA margin toward a MID-CYCLE level (base 16.5%) rather than carrying the FY2025 trough (11.9% statutory / 13.2% underlying) or the FY2018-21 peak (24-29%) forward; the FY2018-25 through-cycle mean EBITDA margin is 20.7%, so base maturity sits well below it to reflect the structurally higher housing-association mix, the Building Safety Levy from autumn 2026 and the 2027 cost-inflation headwind management has flagged. (2) Working capital: a homebuilder's growth CONSUMES cash -- inventories of GBP4.6bn against GBP3.75bn revenue, net of GBP1.2bn payables/land creditors, is ~0.9x revenue of net working capital -- so wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE (-80% of the revenue change in base/bear, -65% in bull where Westbury partnerships and asset-turn improvement lift capital efficiency). In bear years with falling revenue this correctly releases cash, as housebuilders destock in downturns. Year-1 base owner FCF of ~GBP100m is consistent with management's guided year-end net debt/cash range of -GBP100m to +GBP100m after GBP192m of dividends from GBP117m opening net cash. (3) Terminal caps of 12x/14x/15x (bear/base/bull) per the method's 12-15x guidance for cyclicals. (4) Risk charged once: a single 10% GBP WACC, scenarios and weights carry the cycle. ANCHOR TIMING: net debt is taken from the 30 June 2026 balance sheet as the latest filing requires; this is the seasonal working-capital peak (H1 absorbed GBP389m of working capital) and management guides year-end to roughly nil net debt, so the anchor is conservative by roughly GBP100-150m (~30-45p/share) relative to a year-end anchor. EQUITY BRIDGE: deducts the GBP205.6m legacy-buildings (cladding) provision -- cash remediation spend already expensed in prior years and therefore absent from projected EBITDA -- and the GBP128.4m FY2025 final dividend liability at 30 June 2026 (paid July 2026; cash that has left since the anchor date and is not in forward flows). The GBP133.9m defined-benefit pension surplus is NOT added (restricted, not realisable). Land creditors (GBP497.3m) are treated as operating working capital, not debt, matching the company's own net-debt definition; their imputed interest sits below EBITDA. Interest income (GBP11.4m) stripped from the FCF base for a clean unlevered series. SBC kept as an explicit line at ~0.4% of revenue.

equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 note 11: GBP136.7m non-current + GBP68.9m current at 30 June 2026. Cash outflow (GBP24.2m utilised in H1) not captured in projected EBITDA because the cost was expensed in FY2021-25.
H1 FY2026 balance sheet current liability; 40p/share paid 10 July 2026, after the 30 June net-debt anchor date and not in forward flows.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Guidance-anchored base path (FY2026 consensus +7.5%, decelerating to 2.5%; 10-year average 3.9%). Historical CAGRs are unusable as a forward rate: revenue is flat through the cycle (FY2018 GBP3,738m vs FY2025 GBP3,751m), EPS CAGRs measure peak-to-trough, and owner FCF is negative at both 3- and 5-year endpoints (FY2022 GBP352.9m -> FY2025 -GBP38.6m; FY2020 GBP731.3m -> FY2025 -GBP38.6m) so a CAGR is undefined.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.5%/5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from EPS CAGR (-14.9%) and revenue CAGR (2.4%). Cause: GBP2.3bn of dividends paid FY2021-25 (62% of cumulative net income) hold book value flat while earnings fell 55% from the FY2021 peak. Neither series is a usable forward growth rate for a cyclical at a trough.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income), GBPm: FY2018 610.5, FY2019 568.3, FY2020 731.3, FY2021 747.6, FY2022 352.9, FY2023 -190.4, FY2024 26.8, FY2025 -38.6. The collapse from FY2022 is land and WIP investment at the bottom of the cycle (inventories GBP3.4bn FY2022 -> GBP4.5bn FY2025), not operating deterioration: underlying operating profit rose 17% in FY2025. SBC is not growing faster than cash flow in any meaningful sense (GBP6-16m on GBP3.3-3.8bn revenue). FY2018 'EquityAwardTaxes' of GBP159.9m in the KPIs relates to the 2012 LTIP settlement, a one-off, and is excluded from the SBC adjustment.

base.growth_note: FY2026: c.12,500 completions (+5%) at a private ASP up ~3% = ~+7.5% revenue, in line with company-compiled consensus. FY2027-30: outlet growth 273 -> 300 (+10%) plus 2-3% HPI, fading to 2.5% by FY2033.
base.margin_note: FY2026 EBITDA 12.6% = consensus underlying operating profit GBP491m + ~GBP24m D&A on ~GBP4.03bn revenue, with a small allowance for H2 restructuring charges. FY2027 nearly flat on the flagged GBP40-50m cost headwind. Ramp to 16.5% by FY2032 -- a mid-cycle level: 3-4pp below the FY2018-25 through-cycle mean of 20.7% and 3.5pp short of management's 20% housing operating margin ambition.
base.tax_note: UK corporation tax 25% + Residential Property Developer Tax 4% = 29% statutory; FY2024-25 cash tax ran 24-27% of PBT on timing. 27% then 28% flat.
base.wc_note: Net working capital (inventories less payables incl. land creditors) ~0.9x revenue; growth consumes ~80% of each year's revenue increase in land/WIP. Year-1 owner FCF ~GBP100m ties to guided FY2026 year-end net debt/cash of -100 to +100 after GBP192m dividends.

bull.margin_note: Management's 20% housing operating margin ambition reached by FY2032 (EBITDA ~20.5%) via Charles Church mix, strategic-land conversion at ~27% embedded site margins, Brickworks/Space4 cost advantage and operating leverage. Still below the FY2018-19 peak of 28-29%.
bull.wc_note: Capital-light Westbury partnerships growth and improved asset turns lift working-capital efficiency (-65% capture vs -80% base).

bear.growth_note: FY2026 lands at the bottom of guidance (completions ~12,000, softer private sales rate already visible at 0.59/week). A 2027-28 housing downturn on sticky mortgage rates and fiscal tightening takes revenue down ~11% peak-to-trough (FY2023 was -27%; this is a moderate, not GFC-scale, recession), then a slow recovery to trend.
bear.margin_note: Trough EBITDA margin 9% in FY2028 (FY2023 statutory was 13.2% in a mild downturn with incentives and build-cost inflation; 9% assumes heavier incentives, under-recovered fixed costs and NRV write-downs). Recovers only to 12% -- the housing-association mix, Building Safety Levy and unmitigated cost inflation prove structural.
bear.wc_note: Falling revenue in FY2027-28 releases working capital (negative capture on a negative change), which is the realistic destocking behaviour and is why bear-case FCF does not collapse with margins.

scenario_narratives.base: Persimmon delivers the FY2026 consensus (c.12,500 completions, underlying operating profit ~GBP491m) and grows volumes mid-single-digit through outlet expansion from 273 toward 300 and the strategic land bank, with house-price inflation of 2-3%. Margins recover slowly from the FY2025 trough as higher-margin strategic land (embedded site margin ~27%) replaces legacy plots and Charles Church scales, but the 2027 cost-inflation headwind, the Building Safety Levy and a permanently higher housing-association mix hold the mature EBITDA margin at ~16.5%, below the 20.7% through-cycle mean and short of the 20% ambition. Working capital absorbs ~80% of each year's revenue growth, so owner FCF conversion stays well below NOPAT; the GBP205.6m cladding provision is paid down from cash. Terminal value is Gordon at 2% growth, inside the 14x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: The structural undersupply thesis plays out: planning reform (Planning and Infrastructure Act), the GBP39bn Affordable Housing Programme and falling mortgage rates lift completions 7-8% a year through FY2029 while Persimmon keeps taking share from Barratt Redrow, Taylor Wimpey and Vistry on its lowest-in-sector build cost. Charles Church doubles to ~2,000 homes, Westbury grows capital-light, Brickworks capacity expansion and Space4 timber frame absorb cost inflation, and the 20% housing operating margin / 20% ROCE ambition is met by FY2032. Asset turns improve so working capital absorbs only ~65% of growth. Mature margins still sit 8pp below the FY2018-19 peak -- this is a recovery to mid-cycle-plus, not a return to the Help-to-Buy era.
scenario_narratives.bear: Mortgage rates stay sticky, the Autumn Budget's fiscal tightening and the mansion tax dent sentiment, and the softer net private sales rate already visible after H1 FY2026 becomes a 2027-28 downturn: revenue falls ~11% peak-to-trough, incentives rise, the GBP40-50m build-cost headwind lands largely unmitigated, and the EBITDA margin troughs at 9% with NRV provisions and H2 FY2026 restructuring charges. Recovery is slow and partial -- the margin settles at 12% because the housing-association mix, the Building Safety Levy and cladding costs (which could grow if further defects are found) are structural. Destocking releases working capital in the downturn, which keeps FCF positive, but the terminal business is a low-growth, 12%-margin volume builder capped at 12x FCF.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% and bull trimmed from 35% to 25%. Bear: a UK housing downturn within a 10-year window is a base-rate event, not a tail (FY2023 was one, 2008 a severe one), management itself flags a GBP40-50m 2027 cost headwind only half mitigated and a softening private sales rate, and the group has just swung GBP288m from net cash to net debt while carrying a GBP206m cladding liability -- none of which is going-concern risk (GBP1bn committed facilities, GBP3.6bn equity, 1.0x P/B), so bear stops at 25%. Bull needs several independent things to go right at once -- rate cuts, planning reform reaching the ground, Charles Church doubling, and full mitigation of cost inflation to reach the 20% margin -- so it is capped at 25%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A cyclical volume housebuilder valued on mid-cycle owner FCF, not on FY2025 trough earnings and not on the FY2018-21 Help-to-Buy peak. The two judgments that drive the number are the mature EBITDA margin (base 16.5% vs a 20.7% through-cycle mean and management's 20% ambition) and the working-capital intensity of growth (-80% of revenue change), which is why reported FCF has been negative for three of the last four years while underlying profit rose. Intrinsic value lands close to net assets per share (GBP11.25), which is where a housebuilder earning a ROCE near its cost of capital should trade; the bull case is a bet on the 20% ROCE ambition, which would justify a material premium to book, and the bear case is a conventional downturn in which the land bank still holds value. The balance sheet (GBP1bn facilities, negligible debt before the 2026 land investment) means the bear case is a de-rating, not a solvency event.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mature margin assumption: each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly 90-100p/share; the base 16.5% could prove optimistic if housing-association mix and the Building Safety Levy are more structural than assumed, or pessimistic if the 20% ambition is met.

Working-capital capture: if Persimmon sustains the FY2024-26 pace of land and WIP investment beyond the outlet build-out, FCF stays depressed for longer than modelled; conversely a shift to capital-light partnerships would lift conversion.
Cladding remediation liability (GBP205.6m provision) could rise if further defects are identified; it is deducted at book in the bridge with no contingency.
The 30 June 2026 net-debt anchor is the seasonal peak; a year-end anchor would add ~30-45p/share. Deliberately conservative.
UK mortgage rates and fiscal policy drive the cycle timing; the bear path assumes a 2027-28 downturn but the scenario weights, not the WACC, carry that risk.
